record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: Under what data-distribution conditions does a single global federated model outperform independently trained per-client models, how much gain should be expected, and can personalization methods be given guarantees that match or exceed both the purely local baseline and the shared global baseline?

evidence.quote: Thus, a natural theoretical question is to determine under what conditions the shared global model is better than independent per-device models. Suppose we train a model hk for each client k, using the sample of size mk available from that client. Can we guarantee that the model hFL learned via federated learning is at least as accurate as hk when used for client k? Can we quantify how much improvement can be expected via federated leaning? And can we develop personalization strategies with theoretical guarantees that at least match the performance of both natural baselines (hk and hFL)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider a federated learning environment with $K$ clients. Each client $k \in \{1,\dots,K\}$ has access to an i.i.d. sample $S_k = \{z^{(k)}_1,\dots,z^{(k)}_{m_k}\}$ of size $m_k$ drawn from a client-specific distribution $\mathcal{D}_k$ over a common instance space $\mathcal{Z}$. Fix a hypothesis class $\mathcal{H}$ and a loss function $\ell:\mathcal{H}\times\mathcal{Z}\to[0,1]$. For a hypothesis $h\in\mathcal{H}$ define the local population risk $L_k(h) = \mathbb{E}_{z\sim\mathcal{D}_k}[\ell(h,z)]$.

Consider three classes of estimators:
1. The purely local baseline $h_k$, obtained by training only on $S_k$ (e.g.\ empirical risk minimization on $S_k$).
2. The shared global baseline $h_{\mathrm{FL}}$, obtained by federated learning on $\bigcup_k S_k$ (e.g.\ ERM with respect to $\sum_k (m_k/M) L_k$ where $M=\sum_k m_k$, or the output of FedAvg).
3. A personalized estimator $h^{\mathrm{pers}}_k$ that may use both the global aggregated information and the local sample $S_k$.

Let $\rho$ be a chosen notion of dissimilarity between distributions $\{\mathcal{D}_k\}$ (e.g.\ total variation, Wasserstein, or a discrepancy tailored to $\ell$ and $\mathcal{H}$).

Questions. Provide rigorous answers to all three of the following.

(a) Identify explicit, quantitative conditions on $(\rho,\{\mathcal{D}_k\},\{m_k\},\mathcal{H})$ under which, for every client $k$, $\mathbb{E}[L_k(h_{\mathrm{FL}})] \le \mathbb{E}[L_k(h_k)]$, i.e.\ the global federated model is no worse than the purely local model on each client.

(b) Under such conditions, derive a tight (matching upper and lower) bound on the expected improvement $\mathbb{E}[L_k(h_k) - L_k(h_{\mathrm{FL}})]$ in terms of $m_k$, $M$, the complexity of $\mathcal{H}$, and the dissimilarity $\rho$.

(c) Construct a personalization scheme $h^{\mathrm{pers}}_k$ together with a proof that, for every client $k$ and every configuration of $(\{\mathcal{D}_k\},\{m_k\})$,
$$\mathbb{E}[L_k(h^{\mathrm{pers}}_k)] \le \min\bigl(\mathbb{E}[L_k(h_k)],\ \mathbb{E}[L_k(h_{\mathrm{FL}})]\bigr) + o(1)$$
as $m_k,M\to\infty$, with explicit non-asymptotic rates.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial partial progress exists. Fallah, Mokhtari, and Ozdaglar (NeurIPS 2020) develop a MAML-based Per-FedAvg with convergence guarantees in non-convex settings, quantifying performance via TV and Wasserstein distances between client distributions. Subsequent work (e.g., ICLR 2023 personalized FL papers, PeFLL 2023, and many follow-ups) gives further guarantees, but a complete theory giving sharp matching upper and lower bounds and personalization estimators that provably dominate both the local and global baselines uniformly across all heterogeneity regimes remains incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Personalized Federated Learning with Theoretical Guarantees: A Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning Approach
status_evidence.snippet: Performance evaluated in terms of gradient norm for non-convex losses and how it is affected by closeness of underlying user distributions measured by Total Variation and 1-Wasserstein.
status_evidence.claim: Provides theoretical guarantees for a personalized FedAvg variant under distributional closeness assumptions, addressing parts of (a)–(c).

status_evidence.title: Personalized Federated Learning (ICLR 2023)
status_evidence.snippet: Conference paper on personalized federated learning published at ICLR 2023.
status_evidence.claim: Continued active research on personalization with guarantees, indicating the broader question is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: PeFLL: Personalized Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Recent personalized FL approach with analysis.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing development of personalized methods with theoretical analysis.
